title: Commonly Used / Weak Passwords
description: Accounts protected by commonly used, default, or easily guessable passwords enable credential stuffing, brute force, and unauthorized access attacks. Attackers often leverage public password lists or automated tools to gain access, compromising system integrity and confidentiality.
businessImpact: High --- successful exploitation can result in unauthorized access to sensitive data, privilege escalation, lateral movement, disruption of critical systems, and reputational damage to the organization.
remediation:
- Implement strong password complexity policies and minimum length requirements.
- Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users.
- Limit authentication attempts and enforce account lockout thresholds.
- Regularly audit and rotate default or weak credentials.
- Use password managers and encourage user training on secure credential practices.
